prediction.likelyOutcome: Lender is highly likely to prevail on the Guaranty and forbearance-agreement claims; Berger's lack-of-consideration defense is weak given the contemporaneous execution of the Guaranty, his repeated written admissions of validity/default in three forbearance agreements, his express waiver of defenses, and his partial performance (which is hard to square with a claim the obligation never existed). Net recovery should approximate the stipulated Loan A balance plus accrued post-default interest and contractual attorney fees, subject to resolving an internal inconsistency in the record over Loan B's final payoff status.

outcome.description: The trial court granted the lender summary judgment on the guaranty and forbearance agreements; as corrected on limited remand, the judgment awarded $1,091,479 in outstanding principal and $419,226.93 in interest ($1,510,705.93), plus $36,211.50 in attorney fees and $441.75 in litigation expenses. The Eighth District affirmed, rejecting the lack-of-consideration defense.

source.court: Court of Appeals of Ohio, Eighth Appellate District (Cuyahoga County)
